open_decisions.question: BCHCTL00 performs 11 paragraphs that are not in the source (1100-OPEN-FILES, 1200-READ-CONTROL-RECORD, 1300-VALIDATE-PROCESS, 1400-UPDATE-START-STATUS, 2100-READ-CONTROL-RECORD, 2200-CHECK-DEPENDENCIES, 3100-READ-CONTROL-RECORD, 3200-UPDATE-PROCESS-STATUS, 3300-WRITE-CONTROL-RECORD, 4100-UPDATE-COMPLETION, 4200-CLOSE-FILES); the source ends with the comment 'Detailed procedures to be implemented'. Can the complete BCHCTL00 source be supplied, or is the program confirmed unfinished, and if so what must the INIT, CHEK, UPDT and TERM functions do to the batch-control record?

BR-002 states: when WS-PREREQ-MET = 'Y' (PREREQS-SATISFIED) BCHCTL00 returns 0, otherwise warning code 4. The indicator is set only in 2200-CHECK-DEPENDENCIES, which is not in the source. What are the business criteria for a batch job's prerequisites being satisfied? Confirm, correct or reject the stated return-code behaviour.

BR-153: BCHCTL00 sets a process mode (WS-PROCESS-MODE 'I' initialise, 'C' check prerequisites, 'U' update status, 'F' finalise) in every dispatch branch of BR-001, but no statement present tests it. Is the process mode part of the required behaviour (and if so, what does it control), or can it be dropped?

DB2ERR (line 75) uses the non-standard 'ACCEPT WS-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP FROM TIME STAMP'; the ERRPROC logic file flags the same construct (line 57) and PORTDEL uses it for the deletion audit timestamp (source line 169). Which compiler extension is in use and what timestamp format do ERRLOG rows, error-log records and deletion audit records actually carry?

BCHCTL00 performs 11 paragraphs that are not in the source (all OPEN/READ/WRITE/REWRITE/CLOSE of BATCH-CONTROL-FILE, validation, dependency check, completion). What must INIT, CHEK, UPDT and TERM do to the batch control file (open mode, key, fields updated, status codes handled)?

ERRPROC's LINKAGE LS-ERROR-REQUEST is 354 bytes, but DB2ERR (line 199) and DB2STAT (line 227) CALL 'ERRPROC' USING ERR-MESSAGE from copybook ERRHAND (about 370 bytes, different field order). Which layout is the contract of the Java error service?

BCHCON BCT-EMERGENCY is PIC X(8) with VALUE 'EMERGENCY' (9 characters). What initial 8-byte value must the Java constant hold: the compiler-truncated 'EMERGENC', or is the copybook to be corrected (for example a 9-byte field or a different literal)?

Which character encoding (code page) do the files and areas described by these copybooks use for DISPLAY data on the legacy platform (EBCDIC 037, 1140, another EBCDIC variant, or ASCII)? The zoned-decimal test vectors and String codecs depend on it.

Which TRUNC compiler option (STD, OPT or BIN) were the programs including these copybooks compiled with? It decides whether COMP fields such as 9(2) COMP, 9(3) COMP, 9(5) COMP and 9(9) COMP may hold values beyond their PIC digits (up to the halfword/fullword limit), which affects Java range validation and whether 9(9) COMP counters need long instead of int.
